title: 2.1.1: the sweep's safety conditions must be about the worktree they name
description: Six defects found by the phase code review of 2.1.0, three of them data-loss: the sweep acts on a record it did not measure (F244), the standing-in guard is realpath equality rather than containment and cwd_tree fails open (F245), provenance is not bound to the phase or branch it names (F246), a malformed tasks array reads as settled (F247), the panel's git-write never journals and its confirm dialog names nothing (F248), and close-phase's exit codes and stamp ordering are reported but not yet reproduced (F249).
desiredOutcome: Every removal the sweep plans is about the worktree whose provenance, settlement, containment and cleanliness were measured; no precondition fails open; the panel's git-write leaves a journal row and shows the operator what it is about to delete; and each fix carries a case proven red first.
summary: Shipped as 2.1.1. Every removal the sweep plans is now about the worktree whose provenance, settlement, containment and cleanliness were measured - three of the twenty fixes were data-loss defects. `within_tree` was normalising with `os.sep` while git prints `/`, so the containment guard was silently returning on Windows; cases s5b/s5c assert it on every platform now.

tasks.title: F244+F245+F246+F247: the four preconditions must be about the worktree they name
tasks.description: cleanup_plan must act on the measured record, not a re-lookup by branch; standing_in must test containment with an os.sep boundary and longest match; cwd_tree must be three-valued like owned and settled; provenance must compare the phaseId and branch it records; phase_settled must refuse a non-dict task rather than counting it finished.

outcome.summary: F244 the plan acts on the measured record; F245 standing_in is containment with an os.sep boundary and longest match, and cwd_tree is three-valued so 'not asked' refuses; F246 provenance compares the branch it records; F247 an unreadable task entry refuses instead of counting as finished. Every one reproduced first, and every fix reverted to red before it was kept.

verifiedBy: test__worktrees.py w8/w9/w10, s4-s8, pv6-pv9, q6, bd1-bd3

tasks.title: F248: the panel's git-write emits real change rows, journals, and shows what it deletes
tasks.description: Emit {target,field,from,to} rows so the journal, the confirm dialog and appliedDiff all work; redact the worktree path through _journal_io; pass a real cwd_tree; stop inferring both verbs on the dry run; and make SECURITY.md's claim match what the server actually enforces.

outcome.summary: The sweep emits real change rows, so the journal takes them, the confirm dialog names what it is about to delete and appliedDiff can see drift; the worktree is named by basename so a committed journal carries no home directory; the panel passes a real cwd_tree and no longer infers both verbs on a dry run; SECURITY.md now says which half of the dry-run contract the server actually holds.

tasks.title: F249: reproduce and fix close-phase's exit codes, stamp ordering and the -z floor
tasks.description: auto:false must not turn a refusal into exit 0; --no-ff must refuse rather than be dropped on the no-checkout path; mergedAt must be persisted before the cleanup consumes it; an already-contained phase must still be stamped; branch -d after a no-checkout merge must not be a guaranteed refusal; the dry run must preview the cleanup it will really do; and list_worktrees must not require a git newer than Ubuntu 22.04 ships.

outcome.summary: auto:false no longer turns a refusal into exit 0; the stamp is gated on verified containment and runs BEFORE the cleanup, and a failed stamp holds the cleanup back; branch deletion is guarded on the branch's sha instead of git's HEAD-graded branch -d; list_worktrees falls back when -z is refused, so git 2.34 works; --no-ff refuses on the no-checkout path instead of being dropped; --dry-run previews the cleanup.
